_comment: Every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class. Enforced by data_boundary.py from the
fleet-guards checkout named by git config fleet.guards, run from .githooks.
FIXTURE = LIFELIKE test data, whose real counterpart sits in the operator's life and is
structurally indistinguishable from it. Must come from a generator, because a real
record cannot be regenerated, so pasting one in fails at commit.
DATA    = anything a REAL RUN produced. Never in a PUBLIC repo.
This fork (A90ur5/bilibili-cdn-optimizer) does not have the fleet-guards tools, so nothing enforces
this file here: neither CI nor either extension reads it. It is kept, and updated by hand, as the
written record of what may and may not be committed.
_audited: 2026-10-18, second audit, after this fork split the repo into bilibili-cdn-optimizer/ and bilibili-cdn-tw/ and added build and release tooling (the first audit, 2026-09-14, was upstream's, when the repo shipped one script). The question is still not 'is there real output sitting in the tree' but 'CAN shipped code or documentation put real output at a repo-relative path'. The answer is still no, but it is no longer 'there is no filesystem write at all'. Grepped every tracked .js file for writeFile / appendFile / createWriteStream / mkdir / rm / localStorage.setItem / GM_setValue. (1) Three build tools write files, and every byte they write is a deterministic function of committed source: bilibili-cdn-optimizer/tools/build-extension.js writes the userscript copy in chrome-extension/ and chrome-extension.zip; bilibili-cdn-tw/tools/build-extension-tw.js writes chrome-extension-tw/manifest.json, chrome-extension-tw/bilibili-cdn-tw.js and chrome-extension-tw.zip; tools/release.js writes dist/, which .gitignore excludes and .github/workflows/release.yml uploads to a GitHub release. They read only the userscripts, manifests and READMEs, never a browser, a network response or a measurement, and each build's --check (run in CI) proves the committed output equals a fresh build. Their output is therefore TOOL, not DATA. (2) bilibili-cdn-optimizer/bilibili-cdn-optimizer.user.js still has exactly one persistence call, localStorage.setItem(STORE_KEY, ...) at line 121, into the viewer's browser storage on a bilibili origin. (3) bilibili-cdn-tw/bilibili-cdn-tw.user.js persists through GM_setValue (24 call sites), which lands in Tampermonkey's storage or, in the extension build, in the page's localStorage under the 'BiliCDN_TW:' prefix. Both are browser storage and can reach no repo path. (4) bilibili-cdn-optimizer/tools/selftest.js still has one fs call, readFileSync of the userscript under test, and its localStorage stub is an in-memory Map. That is why `data` is empty, and it is a conclusion rather than a default.
_no_companion: This repo has NO private companion, deliberately and not by omission. Both tools keep state only in the viewer's own browser, and none of it is the operator's data to commit. bilibili-cdn-optimizer keeps one JSON object (host, kbps, ts): a CDN hostname and a throughput number. bilibili-cdn-tw keeps more: CDN health and throughput samples, a blacklist and dead-host lists, a probe cache, worker statistics, and an HTTPDNS profile tagged with a 'network key' built from the browser's time zone, language, connection type and downlink. That key is the closest thing in either tool to personal data, since it hints at where and how the viewer connects. It stays in the browser: BiliCDN.diag() and BiliCDN.httpdns() print it to that browser's console, and the script's 'copy diagnostics' report does not include it. If a future version ever records a run to disk, that is the change that has to create a companion, and this key is where to say so.
_fixture_note: `fixture` is empty and that is also audited. bilibili-cdn-optimizer/tools/selftest.js builds its payloads INLINE in code (see payload() and the HOST_FAST / HOST_PREFER constants) rather than loading any file, so there is no fixture file to classify or regenerate. The synthetic host is upos-fast.example.net, inside the synthetic namespace. The other constant, upos-hz-mirrorakam.akamaized.net, is a REAL hostname and is kept on purpose: CFG.PREFER matches the substring 'akamaized.net', so a test that used a made-up domain would not exercise the fallback path at all. It is bilibili's public CDN infrastructure, served to every viewer worldwide, and identifies no person. bilibili-cdn-tw has no tests that load data. The browser tests run while packaging both extensions (Playwright against routed fake bilibili pages) built their payloads inline too, and were not committed.
_measurements_note: bilibili-cdn-optimizer/README.md (moved out of the root README and translated to Traditional Chinese on 2026-10-18) quotes throughput figures measured on the upstream maintainer's own connection (for example 5.8 Mbps during buffer fill versus 195 to 281 Mbps idle). Those are kept because they are the EVIDENCE for design decisions that would otherwise read as taste, and they are aggregate numbers that identify no person and no location. The one sentence that did leak a real circumstance, naming the upstream maintainer's region alongside 'direct connection', was caught by the semantic gate at push time on 2026-09-13 and rewritten before it ever reached the remote; the commit that would have carried it was amended, not followed by a second commit. This fork's own docs (the root README, bilibili-cdn-tw/README.md, both SECURITY-AUDIT.md files and the generated release notes) quote no measurement from the fork operator's connection. Diagnostic output the operator produced while testing, a BiliCDN.diag() dump that included the network key above and a screenshot of the extensions error page, was read in conversation and deliberately not committed; the docs name only generic message types, such as B站's '[Mirror] ... Script error.' log, and generic page types such as /watchlater/list.
_tool_note: Empty, because TOOL is the default class and needs no entry; this list exists only for a hand-written file shaped like a ledger. The nearest candidates added since the first audit are the two SECURITY-AUDIT.md files: dated, hand-written review reports that cite line numbers in the scripts, not records of a run, so they are TOOL by default. The generated extension files and zips are TOOL for the reason given in _audited. Check 4 itself could not be run for this revision, because the fleet-guards tools are not available in this fork; if it ever runs and flags the audits, list them here with that reason.
